problem:
The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064490/assets/dbda6ab548ce83f1b2c2d74cf08c2ec01ea7de089bb36f8e0c98985a432202d1.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=4\cdot 2=8.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-1)\cdot 1-2\cdot 3=-7.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,-7\,|\cdot 8 \\  & =56.\end{aligned}
$$
